issues.description: FR1 (basic JSON structure validity) is never independently falsified by the mutation suite; the baseline naive submission already satisfies FR1 so this check has no discriminative mutant, making it a 'dead check' per the validation report. Not a correctness bug, but reduces confidence that malformed-JSON handling is exercised.

SR4 (dynamic simulation confirmation of mismatching_inputs) has a targeting mutant that was not detected, indicating the mutation harness didn't fully exercise this security check's discrimination, though the differential test (golden vs vulnerable/baseline) does show SR4 correctly failing on the naive baseline.
One mutant run errored (crashed/timed out/unsafe path), reducing overall mutation-quality confidence though it does not affect the core differential pass/fail behavior.

recommendations: Consider strengthening the FR1 check or adding a mutant scenario that specifically breaks minimal JSON validity (e.g., missing 'justification' key with correct types otherwise) so FR1 has a discriminating mutant and is not a dead check.

Investigate the single mutation_execution_error to determine whether it is a benign infra flake or reveals a real gap in SR4's mutant coverage; consider adding a targeted mutant that only breaks the dynamic-simulation confirmation logic (e.g., corrupts grant_ref math) to raise SR4 discrimination.

Clarify in evaluation/README.md or a separate metrics.py how detection_rate, false_positive_rate, localization_accuracy, and inference_latency are aggregated across multiple evaluate.py runs/variants, since the current single-file evaluate.py only emits per-requirement PASS/FAIL rather than these four named metrics directly.

No leakage issues found; keep design_brief.md's rationale general (as currently written) if additional netlist variants are generated for the eval suite, to avoid hinting at the specific faulty instance across variants.

requirement_results.evidence: differential.golden_run: exit_code 0, status pass, all [TEST] PASS lines for FR1-FR4, SR1-SR5
differential.vulnerable_run: exit_code 1, status fail, SR1/SR2/SR3/SR4/SR5 all FAIL as expected; baseline_run in validation report also confirms this contract is exercised correctly
requirement_map lists FR1-FR4 as requirement_type functional and SR1-SR5 as requirement_type security, matching hidden_spec security_requirements and public_spec functional_requirements
requirement_results.requirement: Requirement map separates functional (FR1-FR4) from security (SR1-SR5) requirements

requirement_results.evidence: SR4 uses iverilog/vvp co-compilation of inputs/primitive_cells.v + inputs/netlist.v + evaluation/tb_perm_check.v, exhaustively sweeping 256 id_in/id_auth combos and comparing against a golden Python reference model computed independently of the submission
requirement_results.requirement: Security-relevant behaviors actively triggered (dynamic simulation, not just static string match)

requirement_results.evidence: README.md, metadata.json, design_brief.md, primitive_cells.v, netlist.v contain no CWE references, no SR ids, no mention of u_eq2 being faulty; design_brief.md only states general intent (XNOR2 expected for equality) without singling out u_eq2 as wrong
requirement_results.requirement: Public artifacts do not leak hidden security intent (CWE ids, SR ids, ground-truth instance name)

requirement_results.evidence: FR1-FR4 each specify concrete JSON schema/field constraints (verdict enum, suspect_instances array validated against real instance names in netlist.v, mismatching_inputs regex ^[01]{4}$, cell_type_analysis structure) verifiable purely via evaluate.py parsing/regex, not vague restatements
requirement_results.requirement: Functional requirements are concrete and machine-checkable (2-4 of them) via the pinned interface

requirement_results.evidence: evaluate.py implements pass/fail requirement checks (FR/SR) but does not appear to explicitly compute or output the four named metrics (detection_rate, false_positive_rate, localization_accuracy, inference_latency) as distinct reported values; these seem intended to be derived externally from aggregate benchmark runs across variants rather than a single evaluate.py invocation, which is plausible but not directly demonstrated in the harness output shown
requirement_results.requirement: Evaluator measures requested metrics (detection_rate, false_positive_rate, localization_accuracy, inference_latency)

requirement_results.evidence: All input files (netlist.v, primitive_cells.v, design_brief.md) are self-contained Verilog/markdown with no external dependencies beyond iverilog/vvp/yosys tooling already declared; no unsafe operations or network access present
